title: Make tags that differ only in case one tag

blocks.text: This builds on the previous practice. The tag cloud now shows `Linux`, `LINUX` and `linux` as three tags, and the blog's editors want one, shown the way it was first typed. So the index keeps each tag's text in a `Tag` and uses `Tag`s as the keys of its map; `key(...)` from the previous practice is already there.

Finish `equals` and `hashCode` of `TagIndex.Tag` in `src/main/java/practice/TagIndex.java`: two tags are the same tag when they differ only in case, or in how a device sent their accented letters. The blog runs on servers in several countries, with different default locales. About four lines in total.

cases.says: tags with the same spelling are one tag, shown as first typed, and different tags stay apart
tags that differ only in case are one entry in the index's hash map, and a search in any case finds it
tags that differ only in case are one tag even when the server's default locale is Turkish
whenever two tags are equal, including tags with Turkish i's, a long s or a sharp s, their hash codes are equal
an accented tag in another case and in the other device form is still the same tag

origin.section: equalsIgnoreCase Has No Matching hashCode: Compare and Hash One Key

concepts: toLowerCase() uses the default locale, so a case-insensitive key built with it breaks under a Turkish default, while equalsIgnoreCase and toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) do not.
A hash set or map looks by hashCode before it asks equals, so an equals that ignores case beside a hash of the raw text lets case variants in.
equals and hashCode must use one canonical key, because equalsIgnoreCase's per-code-point fold and toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) disagree on letters such as the dotless i.
